sub_answers.sub_question: What are the dominant experimental systematic uncertainties reported by ATLAS for B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− branching ratios?
How do uncertainties in B-meson production fractions and fragmentation affect ATLAS branching ratio determinations?
What theoretical inputs (e.g., decay constants, form factors) and their uncertainties enter the interpretation of B→μμ results?
How do differences among experiments or analysis methods create tensions or ambiguities in combined B→μμ constraints?
What model-dependent assumptions (e.g., effective operator basis, lepton-flavor universality) lead to ambiguous theoretical interpretations?
What constraints do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on the Wilson coefficients in the effective Hamiltonian for b→sℓℓ transitions?
How have ATLAS results influenced global fits of flavor observables addressing lepton-flavor universality or scalar/pseudoscalar couplings?
Which classes of new-physics models (e.g., supersymmetry, Z′, leptoquarks) are constrained by the ATLAS B→μμ branching fraction measurements?
How are ATLAS B→μμ limits incorporated into combined experimental averages (e.g., by HFAG or PDG) used for model exclusion?
What projected improvements in sensitivity would strengthen constraints on flavor-violating couplings from future ATLAS datasets?
What branching ratio for B_s0 → μ+μ− did the ATLAS collaboration report and in which publication/year?
What branching ratio or upper limit for B0 → μ+μ− did ATLAS report and in which dataset or year?
What are the statistical and systematic uncertainties quoted by ATLAS for these branching ratio measurements?
Which datasets (integrated luminosity, collision energy) and triggers did ATLAS use for the rare B→μμ analyses?
What significance or confidence level did ATLAS report for the observation or exclusion of B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− decays?
What muon identification and reconstruction algorithms does ATLAS employ for low-rate B→μμ decays?
What event selection criteria and multivariate classifiers did ATLAS use to separate signal from background in B→μμ searches?
How does ATLAS model and estimate combinatorial and peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− analyses?
What fitting procedures and likelihood functions does ATLAS use to extract yields and branching fractions for B→μμ?
How are detector acceptance, efficiency, and trigger corrections determined and validated in ATLAS B→μμ measurements?

Which specific detector-related systematics (muon ID/trigger efficiency, mass scale/resolution, pileup, background modeling, fit bias) dominate ATLAS's reported uncertainties on the measured B_s0→μ+μ− and B0→μ+μ− branching fractions, and what are their quoted sizes in the latest ATLAS publication(s)?

Quantify how uncertainties in the b-hadron production fractions (f_s/f_d), fragmentation functions, and B-hadron kinematic acceptance used by ATLAS propagate into the extracted B→μ+μ− branching ratios; which input values and uncertainties (ATLAS vs. LHCb vs. theory) are used?

List the theory parameters (B_s and B_d decay constants, CKM elements, short-distance Wilson coefficients, higher-order QCD/EM corrections, and any needed bag parameters) that feed into the SM prediction and experimental interpretation of B→μ+μ−, and report the individual uncertainty contributions quoted in recent theory/phenomenology papers.

Identify specific cases where ATLAS results differ from LHCb, CMS, or global fits (e.g., central values, confidence intervals, treatment of peaking backgrounds or normalization channels), explain how analysis choices (selection, multivariate methods, normalization to B+→J/ψK+, simultaneous fits) produce those discrepancies, and cite numerical examples.

Which theoretical framework choices (operator basis/assumed effective Hamiltonian, treatment of scalar/pseudoscalar operators, assumptions about lepton-flavor universality or NP phases, and use of SM input values) cause alternative interpretations of the same B→μ+μ− measurement, and how do these assumptions change limits on specific Wilson coefficients or NP models?

What numerical upper/lower bounds (with confidence levels) do the ATLAS B_s0 → μ+μ− measurements place on specific effective Hamiltonian Wilson coefficients—e.g., C10, C10′, C_S, C_S′, C_P, C_P′—and on combinations like C10−C10′ or scalar/pseudoscalar ratios used in b→sℓℓ EFT fits?

By how much have ATLAS B→μ+μ− results shifted central values, uncertainties, pulls or chi-squared in published global flavor fits (for example UTFit, HFLAV/HFAG, or Flavio analyses) that test lepton-flavor universality or constrain scalar/pseudoscalar Wilson coefficients, and which fit parameters saw the largest changes after including ATLAS inputs?

Which specific classes and benchmark realizations of new-physics models are excluded or tightly constrained by ATLAS measurements of B_s→μ+μ− and B^0→μ+μ−—for example MSSM scenarios with large tanβ (specify bounds on tanβ and m_A), Z′ models with flavor-changing b–s couplings (limits on g_bs and M_Z′), and leptoquark representations (e.g., S_3, U_1) with bounds on their masses and Yukawa couplings—and what ranges remain allowed?

Exactly how are ATLAS B→μ+μ− upper limits and measurements incorporated into community combined results and world averages (for example HFLAV/HFAG or PDG): do the collaborations use ATLAS-provided likelihood profiles, Gaussian approximations, treatment of correlated systematics, or rescaling procedures, and how does that influence the published combined branching fractions and uncertainties used for model exclusion?

What are the projected sensitivities from upcoming ATLAS datasets (Run 3, full Run 3 luminosity, and HL-LHC) for B_s→μ+μ− branching fraction and for derived constraints on flavor-violating couplings—quantify expected percentage improvements in branching-fraction uncertainty, projected 95% CL limits on scalar/pseudoscalar Wilson coefficients, and expected reach in model parameters such as lower bounds on Z′ mass vs. coupling or exclusions in tanβ–m_A plane?

Which numerical value for the branching fraction of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- did the ATLAS Collaboration publish, and in which paper or conference note and year was that value reported (provide reference citation or arXiv/DOI if available)?

What branching fraction measurement or upper limit for the decay B^0 → μ^+μ^- did ATLAS report, and in which dataset description or publication year (or dataset period, e.g., Run 1/Run 2, year(s) of data taking) was that result presented?

For the ATLAS B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- and B^0 → μ^+μ^- results, what were the quoted statistical uncertainties and the quoted systematic uncertainties on the branching fractions (give the uncertainties separately and indicate whether they are ±, asymmetric, or 90/95% CL limits)?

Specify the ATLAS datasets used for the rare B→μ^+μ^- analyses: the integrated luminosity(s), proton–proton collision energy (√s) for each dataset, the data-taking periods (years or Run 1/Run 2), and the primary muon or dimuon trigger paths employed in the analysis (e.g., single-muon, di-muon, low-p_T specialised triggers).

What significance values or confidence levels did ATLAS quote for the observation (or lack thereof) of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^- and B^0 → μ^+μ^- decays (report sigma significance for any observed signals and the confidence level for upper limits, e.g., 95% CL limits) and state which result corresponds to which decay?

Which ATLAS muon reconstruction chains (standalone, combined, segment-tagged, calorimeter-tagged) and particle-identification algorithms are used when reconstructing low-rate B→μ+μ− decays, and what track quality, hit and momentum requirements are applied?

What precise event preselection cuts, kinematic and topological variables, and multivariate methods (e.g. BDT, neural networks) did ATLAS train to discriminate B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− signal from backgrounds, and what input variables and training samples were used?

What procedures does ATLAS use to build models for combinatorial background and for peaking backgrounds from misidentified hadronic B decays (e.g. B→hh, semileptonic modes), including control samples, sideband choices, and mis-ID rate measurements?

Which extended/unbinned/binned maximum-likelihood functions, probability density function components (signal shapes, background shapes, mass resolution models), and nuisance-parameter treatments did ATLAS implement to extract signal yields and convert them to branching fractions in B→μ+μ− analyses?

How does ATLAS determine and validate geometric acceptance, reconstruction and selection efficiencies, and trigger efficiencies for B_s0/B0 → μ+μ− (MC corrections, data-driven scale factors, tag-and-probe studies, dependence on kinematics), and how are systematic uncertainties assessed?

Which ATLAS experimental sources of systematic error (trigger efficiency, muon ID/reconstruction, mass-scale calibration, fit model, normalization channel uncertainties, pile-up) contribute most to the measured B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− and B^0 → μ^+μ^− branching-fraction uncertainties, and what magnitudes were quoted in the ATLAS publications or internal notes?

Quantify how uncertainties in b-hadron production fractions (f_s/f_d, f_u/f_d) and fragmentation modeling (PYTHIA tunes, fragmentation functions) propagate into ATLAS determinations of B_s^0 and B^0 → μ^+μ^− branching ratios, and which ATLAS inputs or external measurements were used for those fractions?

Which theoretical inputs used to convert measured signal yields to branching ratios—such as decay constants f_Bs and f_B, CKM matrix elements, lifetime differences (ΔΓ_s), and QED radiative corrections—and their quoted uncertainties appear in ATLAS B→μ^+μ^− analyses or in the theory papers ATLAS cites?

When comparing ATLAS results with CMS, LHCb or global combinations, what methodological differences (normalization channels, blind/unblind procedures, background-model choices, multivariate selection, treatment of peaking backgrounds) and their estimated systematic shifts explain any discrepancies or tensions among B_s^0/B^0 → μ^+μ^− measurements?

What analysis or theoretical assumptions (choice of effective Hamiltonian/operator basis, inclusion/exclusion of scalar or pseudoscalar operators, assumptions about lepton-flavor universality or new physics phases, use of SM branching-ratio SM prediction inputs) introduce model dependence in interpreting the ATLAS B→μ^+μ^− limits and how do these choices change inferred constraints on Wilson coefficients?

What quantitative limits on specific Wilson coefficients (C9, C9', C10, C10', CS, CS', CP, CP') follow from the ATLAS measurement of B_s0→μ+μ−, including the confidence levels and the operator combinations that are most tightly constrained?

In what ways have ATLAS B_s0→μ+μ− results changed global fits performed by groups/tools (for example HFLAV/HFAG, UTFit, CKMfitter, Flavio), particularly regarding lepton-flavor-universality tests (RK, RK*) and fits for scalar/pseudoscalar operator coefficients?

Which explicit new-physics scenarios and parameter regions are ruled out or strongly constrained by the ATLAS B→μ+μ− branching-fraction measurements — for example MSSM/2HDM heavy Higgs contributions, Z′ models with flavour-changing b→s couplings, and specific scalar or vector leptoquark representations — and what ranges of masses/couplings are affected?

How do combined-experiment averages and compilations (such as those provided by HFLAV, PDG, CKMfitter or global-likelihood repositories) incorporate ATLAS B→μ+μ− upper limits/measurements — what combination methods, treatment of systematic correlations, and likelihood inputs are used to produce the consensus branching-ratio values used for model exclusion?

Based on HL-LHC projections, ATLAS upgrade plans, and published sensitivity studies, what improvements in the B_s0→μ+μ− branching-ratio precision and corresponding tightened bounds on flavor-violating Wilson coefficients or mediator couplings are expected at target luminosities (e.g., 300 fb⁻¹, 3 ab⁻¹), and which detector/analysis upgrades drive those gains?
Provide the value ATLAS published for the branching fraction of B_s^0 → μ^+μ^−, citing the specific paper (journal or preprint) and publication year in which that result appears.

State the numerical branching fraction or 95% (or quoted) upper limit for B^0 → μ^+μ^− reported by ATLAS, and specify the analysis dataset or year (e.g., Run 1/Run 2, integrated luminosity period) associated with that number.

List the separate statistical and systematic uncertainty components ATLAS quoted for the measured B_s^0 and B^0 → μ^+μ^− branching fractions (give values and indicate which uncertainty applies to which decay and whether uncertainties are symmetric or asymmetric).

Detail the ATLAS datasets used in the rare B→μμ measurements: for each dataset provide the collision energy (√s), integrated luminosity, data-taking year(s), and any specific trigger selections or muon trigger thresholds cited in the analysis.

Give the reported significance levels or confidence intervals ATLAS quoted for the B_s^0 → μ^+μ^− observation and for limits on B^0 → μ^+μ^− (for example, number of standard deviations, p-value, 90%/95% CL limits), and cite where in the paper these are stated.

Which specific muon reconstruction categories and identification algorithms does ATLAS deploy for rare, low-rate B→μ+μ− searches (e.g., combined, segment-tagged, standalone, calorimeter-tagged), and what quality/vertex-matching, momentum-scale, and low-pT performance criteria or working points are applied to maximize signal efficiency while controlling misidentification?

What exact event preselection cuts, kinematic and vertexing variables, and multivariate classifiers (type of algorithm, input variable list, training samples, and optimization metric) did ATLAS use to discriminate B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− signal from backgrounds, and what cut values or BDT-score operating points were chosen for the published analyses?

What methods did ATLAS use to separate and quantify combinatorial versus peaking backgrounds in B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− searches — specifically, how were sideband interpolation, mass-shape parameterizations, MC templates, and data-driven misidentification rates (e.g., from B→h+h− or B→J/ψX control samples) combined to estimate each background component and its uncertainty?

Which fitting strategies and likelihood constructions did ATLAS employ to extract signal yields and branching fractions for B_s0 and B0 → μ+μ− — for example, unbinned or binned maximum-likelihood fits, simultaneous fits across categories (mass, BDT bins, trigger/eta regions), signal and background PDF choices, nuisance-parameter constraints, and the use of profile-likelihood or frequentist test-statistics to set limits or measure significances?

How did ATLAS determine and validate acceptance, reconstruction and selection efficiencies, and trigger corrections for B_s0/B0 → μ+μ− (e.g., MC-derived acceptance, tag-and-probe scale factors from J/ψ→μ+μ− or Υ→μ+μ−, trigger efficiency maps, and closure tests using normalization channels), and how were associated systematic uncertainties evaluated and propagated into the final branching-fraction results?
